1	# GH3 (Wii) — Navigation Model
2	
3	Working model of Guitar Hero III: Legends of Rock (Wii) screens and the menu
4	graph between them. This is the source artifact for the §4.8 game-state work:
5	the **observer** (M9) classifies the current screen and reads the highlighted
6	selection; the **controller** (M10) plans button sequences along the graph
7	edges below. See [`spec.md`](spec.md) §4.8.3 (game catalog & menu metadata).
8	
9	Screen text is transcribed from operator narration; the referenced screens live
10	as a renamed corpus in [`gh3_screens/`](gh3_screens/) (see its README for the
11	name ↔ original-snapshot mapping). Raw `marvin-perf snapshot` captures land in
12	the gitignored `tools/marvin-perf/snapshots/`. Native capture is 720×480.
13	
14	**Scope now:** the navigation *structure* — screens, their items, and the edges
15	between them. The **vision** side is now built: the observer classifier lives in
16	`game/gameplay_classify.c` (`gp_classify()`), and the controller
17	(`game/game_controller.c`) uses it closed-loop (see Navigator notes below). This
18	doc remains the source artifact for the screen/edge model those consume; screen
19	snapshots stay recorded here as the corpus.
20	
21	Status: **in progress** — this navigation map is populated screen-by-screen
22	(`TBD` = not yet captured); the observer + controller that consume it are built.

24	---
25	
26	## Conventions
27	
28	### Inputs
29	- **Strum up / strum down** — move the selection within a list.
30	- **GREEN** — confirm / enter the selected item.
31	- **RED** — back up one level.
32	
33	(Bit names on the wire are the gameplay fret/strum masks; the controller emits
34	the same bits for menu navigation — the fretboard MCU doesn't distinguish menu
35	from gameplay. §4.8.4.) Some menus also use the `+` button (pause) and possibly
36	others beyond fret/strum; the full controller is actuatable in principle —
37	fauxmote emulates the complete guitar extension incl. `+`/`−` — the actuator
38	command protocol just needs to carry those inputs.
39	
40	### Highlight paradigms
41	How "selected" is presented drives what the observer reads. Two kinds so far:
42	
43	- **static-list** — the list is painted at fixed screen positions; a highlight
44	  moves between rows. Observer reads *which row is lit*. (e.g. `main_menu`)
45	- **fixed-slot** — the selected item sits in a fixed, highlighted slot and the
46	  list scrolls underneath it. Observer reads *what occupies the highlight slot*.
47	  (e.g. `song_select`)
48	
49	### Edge notation
50	An edge is `from → to : [inputs]`. `STRUM_DN×n` means n strum-downs. Moving to
51	list index `i` from the top (index 0) on a static list is `STRUM_DN×i, GREEN`.
52

140	### section_select  *(practice — variable per song)*
141	- **reached from:** `difficulty_select` → GREEN.
142	- **paradigm:** static-list (assumed; confirm).
143	- **items:** **song-dependent** (intro / verse / solo / etc.), but **index 0 is
144	  always "FULL SONG"** — `gh3_screens/section_select__full_song.png`. Only FULL SONG is in scope; other
145	  sections are ignored.
146	- **select FULL SONG:** `STRUM_UP×N, GREEN` — strum up to the **top** of the
147	  list (FULL SONG = index 0), then confirm. Don't assume the cursor enters at
148	  index 0 (may be sticky / land elsewhere); strumming up saturates at the top so
149	  it lands on FULL SONG regardless of entry position. `N` ≥ the longest section
150	  list (or "until the highlight stops moving"). **Assumes no wrap-around** — see
151	  open items; if the list wraps, read the highlight instead.
152	- **back (RED):** `difficulty_select`.
153	- **leads to:** `speed_select`.

178	- **reached from:** `loading`.
179	- **screen:** `gh3_screens/in_song__training.png` (training-mode example).

344	
345	| from | to | inputs | notes |

348	| main_menu | training_menu | `STRUM_DN×4, GREEN` | TRAINING (index 4) |
349	| training_menu | song_select | `STRUM_DN×1, GREEN` | PRACTICE (index 1) |
350	| song_select | part_select | `STRUM_DN×i, GREEN` | song at list index i; shared node. May skip part_select for some songs |
351	| song_select | bonus list | `BLUE` (back: `YELLOW`) | toggles the song list, not a screen change |
352	| part_select | difficulty_select | LEAD `GREEN` / 2nd `STRUM_DN×1, GREEN` | items song-dependent |
353	| difficulty_select | section_select | `STRUM_DN×index, GREEN` | EASY 0 / MEDIUM 1 / HARD 2 / EXPERT 3 |
354	| section_select | speed_select | `STRUM_UP×N, GREEN` | FULL SONG = top (idx 0); strum up to saturate |
355	| speed_select | loading | `STRUM_UP×N, GREEN` | FULL SPEED = top (idx 0); strum up to saturate |
356	| loading | in_song | _(none — wait)_ | transient; auto-advances |
357	| in_song | pause_menu | `+` (guitar plus) | not a fret/strum bit — see caveat |
358	| in_song | practice_end_menu | _(none — song ends)_ | gameplay completes |
359	| pause_menu | in_song | `GREEN` | RESUME (idx 0) |
360	| pause_menu | loading | `STRUM_DN×1, GREEN` | RESTART (idx 1) → replay |
361	| pause_menu | speed_select | `STRUM_DN×3, GREEN` | CHANGE SPEED (idx 3) |
362	| pause_menu | section_select | `STRUM_DN×4, GREEN` | CHANGE SECTION (idx 4) |
363	| pause_menu | song_select | `STRUM_DN×5, GREEN` | NEW SONG (idx 5) |
364	| pause_menu | quit_confirm | `STRUM_DN×6, GREEN` | QUIT (idx 6) → confirm dialog |
365	| quit_confirm | pause_menu | `GREEN` | CANCEL (idx 0) |
366	| quit_confirm | main_menu | `STRUM_DN×1, GREEN` | QUIT (idx 1) — confirm |
367	| practice_end_menu | song_select | `GREEN` | CONTINUE (idx 0) |
368	| practice_end_menu | loading | `STRUM_DN×1, GREEN` | RESTART (idx 1) → replay |

371	| practice_end_menu | main_menu | `STRUM_DN×4, GREEN` | QUIT (idx 4) |

378	## Navigator notes (implementation)
379	
380	> **Implemented (2026-07-02):** the on-device controller is
381	> `firmware/marvin/default/src/game/game_controller.c` — a port of the offline
382	> `tools/gameplay` `NavController`. Triggered by the dashboard START button or the
383	> console `play` command; reads the committed `Selection`; drives the worked path
384	> below closed-loop and hands off to the CV detector at `in_song`. v1 covers the
385	> practice path from a menu anchor (RED→`main_menu`); mid-song `+`/pause recovery is
386	> not wired (the T1S mask path carries no `+`). See the marvin journal 2026-07-02.
387	
388	How the controller (M10) uses this map. Unmapped paths don't need modeling —
389	they're handled by recovery, not enumeration.
390	
391	- **Closed-loop — verify every screen (not a blind macro).** Before issuing a
392	  step's inputs, confirm the observer reports the expected screen; after issuing
393	  them, confirm the expected destination before proceeding. On mismatch, recover
394	  (see below) and re-plan. Never fire a button sequence open-loop and *assume* we
395	  landed where we hoped — drift, sticky defaults, variable/absent screens, and
396	  load times all break that. This is why the observer (M9) gates the controller
397	  (M10). (spec §4.8.1.)
398	- **Stubs / unknown destinations.** Edges marked `TBD` simply have no plan; the
399	  navigator never routes through them. Out-of-scope nodes (`tutorials_menu`) and
400	  any screen the observer doesn't recognize are treated as "unknown state."
401	- **Recovery from unknown state.** RED backs up one level from any menu, so the
402	  generic recovery is *"press RED until a recognized screen appears, then
403	  re-plan."* This gets us un-stuck from a wrong branch without mapping it.
404	- **Top-item selection (`STRUM_UP×N`).** For steps where we always want the top
405	  item (FULL SONG, FULL SPEED), strum up to saturate at the top, then GREEN,
406	  rather than trusting the entry highlight. (Depends on no wrap-around — open.)
407	
408	### Worked path — training run (main-setlist song `i`, difficulty `d`, LEAD)
409	The nominal input plan. Each step runs **gated on a screen check** (verify the
410	expected screen before, confirm arrival after) per the closed-loop rule above —
411	it is not executed as one blind burst. From `main_menu` (if not there, recover
412	with RED first):
413	
414	1. `STRUM_DN×4, GREEN` → TRAINING → `training_menu`
415	2. `STRUM_DN×1, GREEN` → PRACTICE → `song_select`
416	3. `STRUM_DN×i, GREEN` → song at catalog index `i` (Song catalog) → `part_select`
417	4. select LEAD, then GREEN → `difficulty_select`  *(see caveat)*
418	5. `STRUM_DN×d, GREEN` → difficulty `d` (EASY 0 … EXPERT 3) → `section_select`
419	6. `STRUM_UP×N, GREEN` → FULL SONG → `speed_select`
420	7. `STRUM_UP×N, GREEN` → FULL SPEED → `loading` (wait) → `in_song` (gameplay)
421	
422	**Caveat (step 4):** `part_select` items vary per song and the screen may be
423	absent — exactly the case the closed-loop rule handles: after step 3's GREEN,
424	check which screen actually appeared. If it's `part_select`, pick LEAD (read the
425	offered items) and GREEN; if it's already `difficulty_select`, skip step 4. A
426	purely open-loop macro can't do this safely (extra inputs would mis-fire), so
427	until the observer exists, restrict to songs known to show LEAD-at-top. Per-song
428	`parts` metadata lets the planner pre-know the layout either way.
429

20	static int gp_lattice(int j, int lo, int hi, int n)

29	static void gp_region_mean(const uint8_t *frame, int w,
30	                           int x0, int y0, int x1, int y1, float out[3])
31	{
32	    uint32_t sb = 0u, sg = 0u, sr = 0u;
33	    int n = GP_FP_SAMPLES;
34	    for (int jy = 0; jy < n; jy++)
35	    {
36	        int y = gp_lattice(jy, y0, y1, n);
37	        const uint8_t *row = frame + (uint32_t)y * (uint32_t)w * GP_BPP;
38	        for (int jx = 0; jx < n; jx++)
39	        {
40	            int x = gp_lattice(jx, x0, x1, n);
41	            const uint8_t *p = row + (uint32_t)x * GP_BPP;
42	            sb += p[0];
43	            sg += p[1];
44	            sr += p[2];
45	        }
46	    }
47	    float cnt = (float)(n * n);
48	    out[0] = (float)sb / cnt;
49	    out[1] = (float)sg / cnt;
50	    out[2] = (float)sr / cnt;
51	}

55	static float s_fp_f[GP_FP_LEN];

57	int gp_fingerprint(const uint8_t *frame, int width, int height, uint8_t *out)
58	{
59	    if (width != GP_CANON_W || height != GP_CANON_H) { return -1; }
60	
61	    int idx = 0;
62	    for (int r = 0; r < GP_FP_ROWS; r++)
63	    {
64	        int y0 = gp_edge(r, GP_CANON_H, GP_FP_ROWS);
65	        int y1 = gp_edge(r + 1, GP_CANON_H, GP_FP_ROWS);
66	        for (int c = 0; c < GP_FP_COLS; c++)
67	        {
68	            int x0 = gp_edge(c, GP_CANON_W, GP_FP_COLS);
69	            int x1 = gp_edge(c + 1, GP_CANON_W, GP_FP_COLS);
70	            float bgr[3];
71	            gp_region_mean(frame, width, x0, y0, x1, y1, bgr);
72	            s_fp_f[idx++] = bgr[0];
73	            s_fp_f[idx++] = bgr[1];
74	            s_fp_f[idx++] = bgr[2];
75	        }
76	    }

79	    double sum = 0.0;
80	    for (int i = 0; i < GP_FP_LEN; i++) { sum += s_fp_f[i]; }
81	    float mean = (float)(sum / (double)GP_FP_LEN);
82	    double var = 0.0;
83	    for (int i = 0; i < GP_FP_LEN; i++)
84	    {
85	        double d = (double)s_fp_f[i] - (double)mean;
86	        var += d * d;

88	    float std = (float)sqrt(var / (double)GP_FP_LEN);
89	    for (int i = 0; i < GP_FP_LEN; i++)
90	    {
91	        float v = (std > 1e-6f)
92	                ? ((s_fp_f[i] - mean) / std * GP_NORM_STD + GP_NORM_MEAN)
93	                : GP_NORM_MEAN;
94	        long q = lroundf(v);
95	        if (q < 0)        { q = 0; }
96	        else if (q > 255) { q = 255; }
97	        out[i] = (uint8_t)q;
98	    }
99	#else
100	    for (int i = 0; i < GP_FP_LEN; i++)
101	    {
102	        long q = lroundf(s_fp_f[i]);
103	        if (q < 0)        { q = 0; }
104	        else if (q > 255) { q = 255; }
105	        out[i] = (uint8_t)q;
106	    }
107	#endif

115	{

119	        if (out_margin)    { *out_margin = 0; }
120	        return GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN;

123	    int32_t best = INT32_MAX, second = INT32_MAX;
124	    int best_k = -1;

126	    {

128	        int32_t d = 0;

130	        {

132	            d += (diff < 0) ? -diff : diff;
133	        }
134	        if (d < best)        { second = best; best = d; best_k = k; }
135	        else if (d < second) { second = d; }
136	    }
137	
138	    int32_t margin = second - best;
139	    if (out_best_dist) { *out_best_dist = best; }
140	    if (out_margin)    { *out_margin = margin; }
141	
142	    if (best <= GP_CLS_T_ABS && margin >= GP_CLS_T_MARGIN)

145	    }

```text
1	"""Fixed-region colour fingerprint (the Q10 recognizer primitive).
2	
3	A frame is partitioned into a coarse `cols x rows` grid of fixed rectangles; each
4	region collapses to its mean (B,G,R). The fingerprint is the concatenated uint8
5	vector, length `3 * cols * rows`. Coarse averaging is what makes this tolerant of
6	the positional slop introduced by the Wii's analog-component -> HDMI path: a
7	sub-cell shift just moves a few pixels between neighbours and washes out.
8	
9	Two knobs matter for the firmware port (memory-bound on uncached DDR reads — see
10	the plan's hardware-cost section):
11	
12	- `samples_per_region`: None computes a dense mean (touches every pixel ~= a
13	  full-frame scan, ~7-20 ms on the SAM9X75). An integer N samples an N x N lattice
14	  per region instead (~cols*rows*N*N reads total, sub-millisecond), trading a little
15	  estimate noise for speed. The coarse average absorbs that noise.
16	- `normalize`: when True, the vector is standardized to a fixed mean/std per frame,
17	  which cancels the global gain/offset value-slop of the analog path. Raw vs
18	  normalized is chosen empirically in `evaluate.py`.
19	
20	Everything is shaped to port 1:1 to integer C: accumulate pixel sums over fixed
21	rectangles (or fixed sample coords), divide, then an L1 compare downstream.
22	"""
23	
24	from __future__ import annotations
25	
26	from dataclasses import dataclass
27	
28	import numpy as np
29	from PIL import Image
30	
31	CANONICAL_W = 720
32	CANONICAL_H = 480
33	BPP = 3  # BGR
34	
35	# Standardization targets for the normalized variant (uint8 midpoint-ish).
36	_NORM_MEAN = 128.0
37	_NORM_STD = 48.0
38	
39	
40	# Defaults chosen empirically in evaluate.py against the corpus: 12x8 normalized
41	# subsampled gives 96% LOO (= 100% of multi-sample classes) and ~99.8% slop
42	# robustness at ~0.1-0.4 ms on the SAM9X75. Normalization is what buys value-slop
43	# (gain/offset) robustness from the analog-component path.
44	@dataclass(frozen=True)
45	class FingerprintConfig:
46	    cols: int = 12
47	    rows: int = 8
48	    samples_per_region: int | None = 5  # None = dense; N = N x N lattice
49	    normalize: bool = True
50	
51	    @property
52	    def length(self) -> int:
53	        return self.cols * self.rows * BPP
54	
55	    @property
56	    def pixel_reads(self) -> int:
57	        """Pixels touched per classification — the on-device cost driver."""
58	        if self.samples_per_region is None:
59	            return CANONICAL_W * CANONICAL_H
60	        return self.cols * self.rows * self.samples_per_region**2
61	
62	
63	DEFAULT_CONFIG = FingerprintConfig()
64	
65	
66	def _to_canonical(image: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
67	    """Ensure a uint8 HxWx3 array at the canonical 720x480 (resize if needed)."""
68	    if image.dtype != np.uint8:
69	        image = image.astype(np.uint8)
70	    if image.shape[:2] == (CANONICAL_H, CANONICAL_W):
71	        return image
72	    # Defensive only — real captures are already native 720x480. Resize via PIL
73	    # (BGR in, BGR out; channel order is irrelevant to a resize).
74	    im = Image.fromarray(image, mode="RGB")
75	    im = im.resize((CANONICAL_W, CANONICAL_H), Image.BILINEAR)
76	    return np.asarray(im, dtype=np.uint8)
77	
78	
79	def _region_bounds(n: int, extent: int) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
80	    """Split [0, extent) into n contiguous integer spans."""
81	    edges = np.linspace(0, extent, n + 1).round().astype(int)
82	    return [(int(edges[i]), int(edges[i + 1])) for i in range(n)]
83	
84	
85	def _lattice(lo: int, hi: int, n: int) -> np.ndarray:
86	    """n sample coordinates inside [lo, hi), centred in their sub-cells."""
87	    fracs = (np.arange(n) + 0.5) / n
88	    return (lo + fracs * (hi - lo)).astype(int).clip(lo, hi - 1)
89	
90	
91	def fingerprint(image: np.ndarray, config: FingerprintConfig = DEFAULT_CONFIG) -> np.ndarray:
92	    """Compute the fixed-region fingerprint of a BGR frame.
93	
94	    Returns a uint8 vector of length `config.length`, region-major (row 0 first),
95	    each region contributing [B, G, R].
96	    """
97	    img = _to_canonical(image)
98	    ys = _region_bounds(config.rows, CANONICAL_H)
99	    xs = _region_bounds(config.cols, CANONICAL_W)
100	
101	    means = np.empty((config.rows, config.cols, BPP), dtype=np.float64)
102	    for r, (y0, y1) in enumerate(ys):
103	        for c, (x0, x1) in enumerate(xs):
104	            if config.samples_per_region is None:
105	                patch = img[y0:y1, x0:x1, :]
106	            else:
107	                yy = _lattice(y0, y1, config.samples_per_region)
108	                xx = _lattice(x0, x1, config.samples_per_region)
109	                patch = img[np.ix_(yy, xx)]
110	            means[r, c] = patch.reshape(-1, BPP).mean(axis=0)
111	
112	    vec = means.reshape(-1)
113	    if config.normalize:
114	        std = vec.std()
115	        if std > 1e-6:
116	            vec = (vec - vec.mean()) / std * _NORM_STD + _NORM_MEAN
117	        else:
118	            vec = np.full_like(vec, _NORM_MEAN)
119	    return vec.round().clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
120

```text
1	"""Nearest-centroid screen classifier with an UNKNOWN reject rule.
2	
3	Each screen class is represented by one centroid fingerprint (the mean over its
4	corpus samples) — a small fixed-size template, which is the per-state metadata the
5	firmware `gameplay_engine` will eventually carry. Classification is L1 distance to
6	every centroid, argmin, then a two-part accept test:
7	
8	    accept best iff  d_best <= t_abs  AND  (d_second - d_best) >= t_margin
9	
10	Otherwise the result is UNKNOWN. The navigator's recovery path depends on a
11	trustworthy UNKNOWN, so the margin gate (am I *clearly* closer to one class than the
12	next?) matters as much as the absolute gate. All math is integer L1 over uint8
13	vectors, matching the firmware target.
14	"""
15	
16	from __future__ import annotations
17	
18	from dataclasses import dataclass
19	
20	import numpy as np
21	
22	from .fingerprint import FingerprintConfig, fingerprint
23	from .screens import UNKNOWN
24	
25	# Coarse fallback thresholds for the default normalized 12x8 config; callers
26	# should prefer values recommended by `evaluate.recommend_thresholds` for the
27	# actual config in use (distance scale depends on grid size + normalization).
28	DEFAULT_T_ABS = 7000
29	DEFAULT_T_MARGIN = 600
30	
31	
32	@dataclass(frozen=True)
33	class Templates:
34	    ids: tuple[str, ...]
35	    centroids: np.ndarray  # (K, L) uint8
36	    config: FingerprintConfig
37	
38	
39	@dataclass(frozen=True)
40	class Classification:
41	    screen_id: str  # a canonical id, or UNKNOWN
42	    best_id: str  # nearest centroid regardless of reject (for diagnostics)
43	    best_dist: int
44	    second_dist: int
45	
46	    @property
47	    def margin(self) -> int:
48	        return self.second_dist - self.best_dist
49	
50	    @property
51	    def accepted(self) -> bool:
52	        return self.screen_id != UNKNOWN
53	
54	
55	def build_templates(
56	    labelled_fps: dict[str, list[np.ndarray]], config: FingerprintConfig
57	) -> Templates:
58	    """Build per-class centroids from labelled fingerprints (id -> [fp, ...])."""
59	    ids = tuple(sorted(labelled_fps))
60	    centroids = np.empty((len(ids), config.length), dtype=np.uint8)
61	    for i, sid in enumerate(ids):
62	        stack = np.stack(labelled_fps[sid]).astype(np.float64)
63	        centroids[i] = stack.mean(axis=0).round().clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
64	    return Templates(ids=ids, centroids=centroids, config=config)
65	
66	
67	def _l1_to_centroids(fp: np.ndarray, centroids: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
68	    diff = centroids.astype(np.int32) - fp.astype(np.int32)
69	    return np.abs(diff).sum(axis=1)
70	
71	
72	def classify_fp(
73	    fp: np.ndarray,
74	    templates: Templates,
75	    t_abs: int = DEFAULT_T_ABS,
76	    t_margin: int = DEFAULT_T_MARGIN,
77	) -> Classification:
78	    """Classify a precomputed fingerprint against templates."""
79	    dists = _l1_to_centroids(fp, templates.centroids)
80	    order = np.argsort(dists, kind="stable")
81	    best_i = int(order[0])
82	    best_d = int(dists[best_i])
83	    second_d = int(dists[order[1]]) if len(order) > 1 else (best_d + t_margin)
84	    best_id = templates.ids[best_i]
85	
86	    accept = best_d <= t_abs and (second_d - best_d) >= t_margin
87	    return Classification(
88	        screen_id=best_id if accept else UNKNOWN,
89	        best_id=best_id,
90	        best_dist=best_d,
91	        second_dist=second_d,
92	    )
93	
94	
95	def classify_image(
96	    image: np.ndarray,
97	    templates: Templates,
98	    t_abs: int = DEFAULT_T_ABS,
99	    t_margin: int = DEFAULT_T_MARGIN,
100	) -> Classification:
101	    """Classify a raw BGR frame (fingerprints it with the templates' config)."""
102	    fp = fingerprint(image, templates.config)
103	    return classify_fp(fp, templates, t_abs=t_abs, t_margin=t_margin)
104

1	"""Canonical GH3 screen identifiers and the corpus filename -> id mapping.
2	
3	Single source of truth aligning the prototype's screen ids with the screen names
4	in `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_navigation.md`. The classifier emits one of these ids
5	(or the sentinel UNKNOWN); the firmware `gameplay_engine` port will reuse the same
6	names.
7	
8	Corpus files are named `<prefix>__<selection>.png` (or just `<prefix>.png` for
9	single-shot screens). The screen *class* is the prefix; the selection suffix is
10	the highlighted item, which a later slice (the highlight reader) handles. Two
11	prefixes are renamed here to match the nav-doc node names.
12	"""
13	
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	# Sentinel for "no recognized screen" — the navigator's recovery path keys off it.
17	UNKNOWN = "unknown"
18	
19	# Canonical screen ids, matching the gh3_navigation.md catalog. Order is the
20	# nominal practice-run flow, then the overlays/dialogs.
21	SCREEN_IDS: tuple[str, ...] = (
22	    "main_menu",
23	    "training_menu",
24	    "tutorials_menu",
25	    "song_select",
26	    "part_select",
27	    "difficulty_select",
28	    "section_select",
29	    "speed_select",
30	    "loading",
31	    "in_song",
32	    "in_song_2p",
33	    "pause_menu",
34	    "quit_confirm",
35	    "practice_end_menu",
36	)
37	
38	# Corpus filename prefixes whose canonical id differs from the prefix itself.
39	# Everything else maps by identity.
40	_PREFIX_RENAMES: dict[str, str] = {
41	    "difficulty": "difficulty_select",
42	    "speed": "speed_select",
43	}
44	
45	
46	def screen_id_for_filename(filename: str) -> str:
47	    """Map a corpus PNG filename to its canonical screen id.
48	
49	    `main_menu__training.png` -> `main_menu`; `difficulty__hard.png` ->
50	    `difficulty_select`; `loading.png` -> `loading`. Raises ValueError if the
51	    resulting id isn't a known screen.
52	    """
53	    stem = filename.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
54	    if stem.endswith(".png"):
55	        stem = stem[: -len(".png")]
56	    prefix = stem.split("__", 1)[0]
57	    screen_id = _PREFIX_RENAMES.get(prefix, prefix)
58	    if screen_id not in SCREEN_IDS:
59	        raise ValueError(f"{filename!r}: unknown screen prefix {prefix!r}")
60	    return screen_id
61

1	"""2-player amp scoreboard location (per-side chrome registration).
2	
3	Two-player GH3 shows two amp scoreboards near the top of the frame instead of the
4	single bottom-left block the score/multiplier/streak readers use. This module
5	locates each amp independently so the (later) 2-player digit/multiplier/streak
6	readers can sample fixed offsets inside a registered block — the register-once
7	design of the single-player score block (`score.py`), but per side and at the
8	2-player scale.
9	
10	The amp is static on screen (fixed rig), so one reference frame builds the chrome
11	reference and registration only absorbs minor per-rig offset. The fiducial is the
12	static dark panel texture, marked by a hand-painted magenta mask
13	(`amp2p_<side>_mask.png`); the digit strip and medallion interior are excluded
14	because they change with the score / multiplier / portrait. Matching is masked,
15	per-frame-normalized SAD over an integer offset search (mirrors `calibrate_score`).
16	"""
17	
18	from __future__ import annotations
19	
20	from dataclasses import dataclass
21	
22	import numpy as np
23	
24	from .corpus import load_bgr, score_corpus_dir
25	from .metadata import AMP2P_BLOCK
26	
27	SIDES = ("left", "right")
28	
29	_LUMA_W = np.array([29, 150, 77], dtype=np.float64)  # BGR weights (matches score.py)
30	
31	
32	def _mask_path(side: str):
33	    return score_corpus_dir() / f"amp2p_{side}_mask.png"
34	
35	
36	def _ref_path(side: str):
37	    return score_corpus_dir() / f"amp2p_{side}_ref.png"
38	
39	
40	def load_amp2p_mask(side: str) -> np.ndarray:
41	    """Load the hand-painted registration mask as a (block_h, block_w) bool array.
42	
43	    Magenta pixels mark the static chrome used for registration. The PNG may be at
44	    any integer upscale of the block; it is box-averaged down to block resolution.
45	    """
46	    x0, y0, x1, y1 = AMP2P_BLOCK[side]
47	    bw, bh = x1 - x0, y1 - y0
48	    a = load_bgr(_mask_path(side))  # magenta is channel-symmetric, so BGR/RGB moot
49	    mag = (a[..., 0] > 200) & (a[..., 2] > 200) & (a[..., 1] < 150)
50	    H, W = mag.shape
51	    if H % bh or W % bw:
52	        raise ValueError(f"amp2p {side} mask {W}x{H} is not an integer multiple of block {bw}x{bh}")
53	    fy, fx = H // bh, W // bw
54	    return mag.reshape(bh, fy, bw, fx).mean(axis=(1, 3)) >= 0.5
55	
56	
57	def _block_luma(image: np.ndarray, side: str, dx: int = 0, dy: int = 0) -> np.ndarray:
58	    """Float luma of the side's block at its nominal position shifted by (dx, dy)."""
59	    x0, y0, x1, y1 = AMP2P_BLOCK[side]
60	    return image[y0 + dy:y1 + dy, x0 + dx:x1 + dx].astype(np.float64) @ _LUMA_W
61	
62	
63	def _norm_masked(a: np.ndarray, mask: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
64	    """Zero-mean/unit-std over the masked pixels (cancels A2D gain/offset)."""
65	    m = a[mask]
66	    return (a - m.mean()) / (m.std() + 1e-6)
67	
68	
69	@dataclass(frozen=True)
70	class AmpReference:
71	    side: str
72	    ref: np.ndarray   # (block_h, block_w) reference luma
73	    mask: np.ndarray  # (block_h, block_w) bool: static-chrome registration pixels
74	
75	
76	@dataclass(frozen=True)
77	class AmpCalibration:
78	    side: str
79	    dx: int = 0
80	    dy: int = 0
81	
82	
83	def build_reference(side: str, images: list[np.ndarray] | None = None) -> AmpReference:
84	    """Build a side's chrome reference (mask + reference luma).
85	
86	    With no `images`, the reference luma is the committed clean crop
87	    (`amp2p_<side>_ref.png`, block-sized). Given full frames, it is their median
88	    block luma at the nominal position (the masked panel is static across frames,
89	    so the median cleans up the unmasked digit/portrait content).
90	    """
91	    mask = load_amp2p_mask(side)
92	    if images:
93	        ref = np.median(np.stack([_block_luma(im, side) for im in images]), axis=0)
94	    else:
95	        crop = load_bgr(_ref_path(side)).astype(np.float64) @ _LUMA_W
96	        ref = crop
97	    return AmpReference(side=side, ref=ref, mask=mask)
98	
99	
100	def calibrate(
101	    side: str,
102	    images: list[np.ndarray],
103	    reference: AmpReference,
104	    search: int = 8,
105	) -> AmpCalibration:
106	    """Lock the side's block offset for this rig by matching the static chrome.
107	
108	    Over an integer offset search, sum the masked per-frame-normalized SAD between
109	    each frame's block and the reference across all frames; the `(dx, dy)` with the
110	    smallest total wins. Run once at gameplay start.
111	    """
112	    ref_n = _norm_masked(reference.ref, reference.mask)
113	    best: tuple[float, int, int] | None = None
114	    for dy in range(-search, search + 1):
115	        for dx in range(-search, search + 1):
116	            total = 0.0
117	            for img in images:
118	                tn = _norm_masked(_block_luma(img, side, dx, dy), reference.mask)
119	                total += float(np.abs((tn - ref_n)[reference.mask]).sum())
120	            if best is None or total < best[0]:
121	                best = (total, dx, dy)
122	    assert best is not None
123	    return AmpCalibration(side=side, dx=best[1], dy=best[2])

This bit once the app passed `0x100000-0x40000 = 0xC0000` (768 KiB); it was intermittent because a prior chip-erase leaves those pages `0xff`.
152:2. **Double DDR init corrupts the MPDDRC (halfword shift).** Even with (1) fixed, u-boot loaded but never ran — total console silence. Root cause: the looping NAND bootstrap **already initializes DDR3L** (it must, to copy the app to `0x23f00000`), and `erase-nand.cfg`'s PC-based heuristic mis-classified it as "DDR cold" (the bootstrap is caught in **SRAM**, `pc 0x301068`) and ran bootstrap-none, whose DDR init re-trained an already-live MPDDRC → mistrained. **Verified**: probing DDR right after `reset init` *without* bootstrap-none read back clean (`deadbeef 12345678`). Fixed by replacing the PC test with a direct DDR round-trip probe — reuse existing DDR when the probe passes, run bootstrap-none only when it fails. Erase then succeeded (`nand erase.chip`, boot region all-`0xff`).

Active render path is **CPU software** (`leRenderer_FillArea` → `_RGBBlendFill`; glyphs too) into a **scratch buffer**, then **`DRV_GFX2D_Blit`** (the SAM9X75 2D engine) copies scratch→framebuffer. The framebuffer is non-cached (`FB_CACHE_NC` → `.region_nocache`) but the Legato scratch was **cacheable**: `LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR` was an empty no-op `#define` and `LE_COHERENT_ATTR = CACHE_ALIGN` (alignment only). The blit's `dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr` of the cached scratch is insufficient on ARM926 → the 2D engine reads stale CPU-cached lines → streaky, cache-line-granularity bleed. **Fix:** define `LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR = __attribute__((section(".region_nocache")))` in **`user.cmake`** (the `#ifndef` guard in the generated `legato_renderer.c` lets the `-D` win → survives MGS regen, no generated-tree patch); MCC grew `ram_nocache` 16→32 MB to host it (ddram.ld + plib_mmu.c + `DDRAM_NO_CACHE_SIZE`). **Confirmed on hardware** (commits `d36640f` + `c0f316c`). **Two upstream Microchip Legato/gfx bugs to file:** (1) with "Cacheable Frame Buffers" **off**, the generator non-caches the framebuffer but leaves the Legato render scratch cacheable (`LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR` empty) — the gap that bit us; (2) `DRV_GFX2D_Fill` omits the `dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr` that `DRV_GFX2D_Blit` has (latent — bites any GPU-fill config, e.g. `LE_WIDGET_BUFFER_ENABLE=1`). | Root-caused by elimination, not by reading (every software-logic path traced correct): a bare opaque magenta fill still bled, hiding the dashboard cleared it, and non-cached scratch fixed it → it's the cached-scratch ↔ 2D-engine coherency, below the software layer. Non-cached is the correct policy on this SoC — Microchip already chose it for the framebuffer (`FB_CACHE_NC`) rather than trusting cache maintenance for a DMA-/GPU-read buffer; the scratch is the same kind of buffer and should match. Adding cache maintenance to `DRV_GFX2D_Fill` would *not* fix this (Fill isn't on the path; the on-path `Blit` already invalidates and still leaked). System-wide rule for this board: any buffer the 2D engine or display DMA reads must be non-cached (or carry correct, sufficient maintenance — which the cacheable path here does not). |

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-15 18:47:08Z)**_

I've now traced the full path. Here's the review of how gameplay screens are identified and why 2-player is the shaky one.

## One mechanism for every screen: a whole-frame fingerprint

There is no per-screen "look here" logic. Every screen — menu or gameplay — is classified the exact same way ([gameplay_classify.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/game/gameplay_classify.c), ported from [fingerprint.py](tools/gameplay/gameplay/fingerprint.py) / [classifier.py](tools/gameplay/gameplay/classifier.py)):

1. Partition the whole 720×480 frame into a fixed **12×8 = 96-region grid** ([gameplay_metadata.h](firmware/marvin/default/src/game/gameplay_metadata.h#L12-L16): `GP_FP_COLS 12`, `GP_FP_ROWS 8`).
2. Each region → mean BGR over a 5×5 sample lattice → a 288-value vector.
3. Per-frame normalize to mean 128 / std 48 (cancels the analog-component→HDMI gain/offset slop).
4. Compare by **L1 distance to one centroid per screen** (the centroid = mean fingerprint over that screen's corpus frames), pick nearest.
5. Accept only if `best ≤ t_abs (9487)` **and** `margin = second−best ≥ t_margin (664)`; otherwise `GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN`.

So the "areas we're looking at" are **all 96 cells of the entire frame, weighted equally** — for menus and gameplay alike.

## Why this is solid for menus and fragile for gameplay

**Menus** are near-static: only the highlight moves, and it touches a handful of the 96 cells. The fingerprint is nearly constant frame-to-frame → tiny in-class spread → locks tightly to its centroid. Exactly what you observed ("fixed in content other than selection").

**Gameplay** breaks the core assumption — the centroid treats the *whole frame* as signal, but most of a gameplay frame is transient:
- two scrolling note highways (2p) / one (1p), animated crowd/stage, star-power + rock meters, changing score/amp digits — all dynamic;
- genuinely fixed elements are only a few: the note-target gem row(s) at the bottom of each highway, the scoreboard chrome, and the highway/lane layout.

The `in_song_2p` centroid was built from **5 frames from a single capture session** (`in_song_2p__{0200..0203,web0714}.png`) — one song, one stage. That centroid bakes *that match's* transient content in as if it were the screen's identity. On a live game, a different venue/character (and just notes sweeping past) shifts many of the 96 cells, L1 grows, and intermittently either crosses `t_abs` or collapses the margin below `t_margin` → **UNKNOWN dropout**. And `t_abs`/`t_margin` are single global scalars dominated by the static menu classes; the dynamic classes' true in-class spread is unmeasured (5 near-identical frames wildly underestimate it).

This isn't a surprise — the journals already flag it twice as open items:
- gameplay journal [journal.md:210-213](tools/gameplay/docs/journal.md#L210): *"the gameplay classifier may need a discriminative fixed region (the invariant 5-colour note-target row) rather than a whole-frame centroid."*
- [journal.md:246-247](tools/gameplay/docs/journal.md#L246): *"only 5 labelled 2P frames, and they're from one capture session — capture more across songs/stages to measure real in-class spread."*

## The useful part: we already know where the fixed elements are

The detector and scoreboard work have already hand-located the invariant regions that the classifier ignores:
- **Note-target rows** — `CV_MARVIN_CFG_1P` / `CV_MARVIN_CFG_2P_LEFT` sense/strike ROIs ([cv_marvin_v1](firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.h)).
- **2p amp scoreboard chrome** — the static-panel masks in [amp2p.py](tools/gameplay/gameplay/amp2p.py) + `AMP2P_BLOCK` (two panels top-left/top-right = the 2p layout signature).
- **1p score block chrome** — `SCORE_CHROME_BOX` in [metadata.py](tools/gameplay/gameplay/metadata.py#L183).

The distinguishing fact for 1p-vs-2p is **layout, not art**: one centered highway + one bottom-left score block, versus two side-by-side highways + two top amp panels. Layout is fixed; stage art is not. A robust classifier for the gameplay screens should key on that structure, not a whole-frame average.

## Where I'd go next

Three directions, cheapest first:

1. **Measure reality first** — capture real 2p frames across several songs/stages/characters, run them through the current classifier, and look at the actual `best_dist`/`margin` distribution vs the 9487/664 gates. This confirms the diagnosis and tells us how bad the spread really is. (Cheap; the journal already asks for it.)
2. **Region-masked centroid for the dynamic classes** — keep the existing 96-cell machinery but add a per-class cell mask so `in_song`/`in_song_2p` only compare the *invariant* cells (highway target row, scoreboard chrome, lane dividers) and ignore crowd/note-scroll/digit cells. Small change to the export + the L1 loop; fits the current design.
3. **Structural gameplay discriminator** — explicitly detect "two highways + two amp panels" vs "one highway + one score block" as a layout test. Most robust, most work.

I have the numbers I need. Here's the honest cost picture.

## The masked scoreboard test is cheap — same ballpark as the current fingerprint

Each amp block is **68×78 = 5,304 px** (`AMP2P_BLOCK`: left `(128,164,196,242)`, right `(515,164,583,242)`), and the hand-painted static-chrome mask keeps **~1,338 px per side** (journal). The 1p block (`SCORE_CHROME_BOX` `(127,311,190,397)` ≈ 63×86) is similar.

You have to separate two very different operations that `amp2p.py` currently bundles:

| Operation | What it costs | When it runs |
|---|---|---|
| **Presence test** (is the chrome here? → gameplay + 1p/2p) | touch only the masked pixels: ~1,338 px × 3ch × 2 sides ≈ **8k DDR reads** + a couple k integer ops + one `sqrt` per side for the normalize | **per frame** |
| **Registration** (`calibrate`, ±8 offset search to pixel-locate the block for digit reading) | 17×17=289 offsets × masked SAD × 2 sides ≈ **~2M reads** | **one-shot** at gameplay entry (and only needed for reading digits, not for classifying) |

For reference, the existing whole-frame fingerprint is 12×8×5×5 = 2,400 samples × 3ch ≈ **7,200 reads**, quoted at ~0.1–0.4 ms on the SAM9X75. So the **per-frame presence test is the same order of magnitude** — sub-millisecond — and you can drop it well below the current fingerprint by subsampling the mask (a few hundred masked px per side is plenty to threshold present/absent). It is *not* heavy.

The key correction to the earlier plan: the per-frame test needs **no offset search**. The rig doesn't move mid-song, so you register once (or just trust the nominal offset — a present/absent threshold tolerates a few px of slop without any search), then every frame is a single masked normalized SAD at the locked offset. The ~2M-read search is a one-time thing and only exists to pixel-align digit cells.

## You're right that highways are irrelevant to *classification*

The highways belong to the note **detector** (`cv_marvin_v1`), a separate subsystem. For the **screen classifier**, the scoreboard chrome answers everything the classifier needs:

- **gameplay vs not** — chrome present at those coords or not;
- **1p vs 2p** — one bottom-left block (`SCORE_CHROME_BOX`) vs two top panels (`AMP2P_BLOCK` left+right).

That's pure layout, which is fixed, instead of a whole-frame average dominated by transient stage/crowd/note-scroll. So the clean architecture is:

- **Keep the whole-frame centroid classifier for the static screens** (menus, loading, pause, quit) — they already classify ~100%; don't disturb them.
- **Replace the two flaky gameplay centroids** (`in_song`, `in_song_2p`) with the masked scoreboard-presence test. Highways never enter the classifier.

## Two things to validate before I trust it

1. **False positives on non-gameplay screens** — confirm no menu/loading frame has dark-panel texture at `(128,164)` / `(515,164)` / `(127,311)` that could clear the SAD threshold. Corpus check.
2. **Pause overlay** — GH3's pause dims the gameplay frame but the amp panels may still be visible behind it, so "scoreboard present" alone could read `pause_menu` as `in_song`. Fix is easy — keep `pause_menu` on its distinctive whole-frame centroid and let it win — but I want to see it in the data.

Concrete next step, all host-side and cheap: run the masked-SAD presence test over the corpus (the 5 2p frames, the 1p frame, all menu/loading/pause frames) and print the SAD-present-vs-absent separation, so we see the actual margin before writing any firmware. ```python
"""Offline evaluation of scoreboard-chrome presence as the gameplay-screen test.

Idea under test: a gameplay screen is identified not by a whole-frame centroid
(flaky — most of the frame is dynamic) but by the presence of its static scoring
chrome. 1-player shows one bottom-left score block (score.py / SCORE_CHROME_BOX);
2-player shows two top amp panels (amp2p.py / AMP2P_BLOCK). This script runs three
masked, per-frame-normalized SAD probes over the whole labelled corpus and reports
the SAD-per-masked-pixel distribution per screen class, so we can see whether
"present" (gameplay) separates from "absent" (menus/loading/pause).

Probes (each = min masked normalized SAD over a small integer offset search, then
divided by the masked-pixel count so the three probes are comparable):
  1p  — score chrome block   (reference = median of the 1p score corpus)
  2pL — left amp panel       (reference = committed amp2p_left_ref crop)
  2pR — right amp panel      (reference = committed amp2p_right_ref crop)

Run: uv run python scan_scoreboard_presence.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

from gameplay import amp2p, score
from gameplay.corpus import load_corpus, load_score_corpus

SEARCH = 4  # integer offset search radius (±SEARCH in x and y)


def _min_sad_per_px(block_luma_fn, ref_n, mask) -> float:
    """min over the offset search of masked normalized SAD, per masked pixel."""
    npix = int(mask.sum())
    best = None
    for dy in range(-SEARCH, SEARCH + 1):
        for dx in range(-SEARCH, SEARCH + 1):
            tn = score._norm_masked(block_luma_fn(dx, dy), mask)
            sad = float(np.abs((tn - ref_n)[mask]).sum())
            if best is None or sad < best:
                best = sad
    return best / npix


def build_probes():
    # 1p score chrome reference from the labelled 1p score corpus.
    score_imgs = [s.image for s in load_score_corpus()]
    if not score_imgs:
        raise SystemExit("no 1p score corpus frames found (data/scores/score__*.png)")
    chrome = score.build_chrome_reference(score_imgs)
    ref1p_n = score._norm_masked(chrome.ref, chrome.mask)

    # 2p amp references from the committed clean crops.
    refL = amp2p.build_reference("left")
    refR = amp2p.build_reference("right")
    refL_n = amp2p._norm_masked(refL.ref, refL.mask)
    refR_n = amp2p._norm_masked(refR.ref, refR.mask)

    def probe(img):
        p1 = _min_sad_per_px(lambda dx, dy: score._block_luma(img, dx, dy), ref1p_n, chrome.mask)
        pl = _min_sad_per_px(lambda dx, dy: amp2p._block_luma(img, "left", dx, dy), refL_n, refL.mask)
        pr = _min_sad_per_px(lambda dx, dy: amp2p._block_luma(img, "right", dx, dy), refR_n, refR.mask)
        return p1, pl, pr

    return probe


def main():
    probe = build_probes()

    # Group every corpus frame by class; fold the 54 score frames in as in_song.
    samples = load_corpus() + load_score_corpus()
    by_class: dict[str, list[tuple[float, float, float]]] = {}
    for s in samples:
        by_class.setdefault(s.screen_id, []).append(probe(s.image))

    def fmt(vals):
        a = np.array(vals)
        return f"{a.min():6.2f} {np.median(a):6.2f} {a.max():6.2f}"

    print(f"SAD-per-masked-pixel (min over ±{SEARCH} offset search). Lower = chrome present.\n")
    print(f"{'screen':<20} {'n':>3}   {'1p  min/med/max':>21}   {'2pL min/med/max':>21}   {'2pR min/med/max':>21}")
    print("-" * 96)
    for sid in sorted(by_class):
        rows = by_class[sid]
        p1 = [r[0] for r in rows]
        pl = [r[1] for r in rows]
        pr = [r[2] for r in rows]
        print(f"{sid:<20} {len(rows):>3}   {fmt(p1):>21}   {fmt(pl):>21}   {fmt(pr):>21}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

The separation is decisive. Reading the table (normalized SAD per masked pixel — **~0.0 = chrome present, ~1.0 = unrelated**, since each block is per-frame zero-mean/unit-std):

| screen | 1p probe | 2pL | 2pR | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **in_song** (1p) | **0.03** | 1.11 | 1.13 | 1p block fires, amps absent ✓ |
| **in_song_2p** | 0.96–1.02 | **0.00–0.04** | **0.00–0.04** | both amps fire, 1p absent ✓ |
| pause_menu | 0.62 | 0.99 | 1.01 | all absent ✓ (see below) |
| quit_confirm | 0.62 | 0.99 | 1.01 | all absent ✓ |
| song_select (64) | 0.92–1.13 | 0.96–1.08 | 0.93–1.19 | all absent ✓ |
| all other menus/loading | 0.90–1.14 | 0.90–1.13 | 1.01–1.19 | all absent ✓ |

**Present vs absent gap is ~15×:** every gameplay match is ≤ **0.04**; the lowest non-gameplay value anywhere is **0.62**. A threshold of τ ≈ 0.3 (anywhere from 0.1 to 0.5) cleanly separates them — a far wider margin than the whole-frame centroid ever had. And 1p vs 2p is unambiguous and mutually exclusive: bottom block fires for 1p, both top amp panels fire for 2p, never both.

**The pause-overlay edge case I flagged shows up and is safe:** `pause_menu` and `quit_confirm` read 0.62 on the 1p probe (vs 0.9+ for other menus) — the score chrome *is* partially visible behind the dimmed pause overlay. But 0.62 ≫ 0.04, so a probe-first classifier never mistakes pause for gameplay. Confirmed in data, not just hoped.

## What this validates and the remaining data gaps

The direction is sound: **scoreboard-chrome presence identifies the gameplay screens with a huge margin, no highways involved.** Three honest gaps, all data (not algorithm):

1. **2p breadth** — the 5 2p frames are one session, and the amp reference is a crop of one of them (in-sample → the ~0.00 is optimistic). The design (static amp chrome) is exactly what should generalize, but real robustness needs more 2p captures across songs/stages/characters.
2. **1p modes** — only 1 full-frame 1p sample (`in_song__training`). The block chrome is mode-independent per the score work, so low risk, but career/quickplay full frames would confirm.
3. **2p pause** — no 2p-pause frame in the corpus, so whether the amp panels persist (dimmed) behind a 2p pause is unmeasured. Worth a capture.

## Two more things to nail down offline before any firmware

Since we're validating everything offline first:

- **A2D-slop robustness** — the per-frame normalize should cancel the analog gain/offset by construction, but the project's convention is to prove it with `perturb.py`. I can perturb the gameplay frames (gain/offset sweeps) and confirm the probe SAD stays ≪ τ, mirroring how the whole-frame classifier was validated.
- **Lock the threshold** — pick τ from these numbers with a documented rule (e.g. midway in log-space between worst-present and best-absent), the same way `recommend_thresholds` sets `t_abs`/`t_margin`.

Want me to run the slop-robustness pass and settle the threshold next — still all offline — and then we design the firmware port (bake the three references into `gameplay_metadata.h` + an integer masked-SAD probe, probe-first with the centroid handling the static screens)?

9	- **positional slop** — sub-cell translation, slight scale (overscan in/out).
10

12	`envelope()` yields a fixed, named battery used by `evaluate.py`.

15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	from collections.abc import Iterator
18	
19	import numpy as np

21

24	    return np.clip(img.astype(np.float32) * gain, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)

26	
27	def adjust_offset(img: np.ndarray, offset: float) -> np.ndarray:
28	    return np.clip(img.astype(np.float32) + offset, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
29	
30	
31	def add_noise(img: np.ndarray, sigma: float, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
32	    noise = rng.normal(0.0, sigma, size=img.shape)
33	    return np.clip(img.astype(np.float32) + noise, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
34	
35	
36	def translate(img: np.ndarray, dx: int, dy: int) -> np.ndarray:
37	    """Shift by (dx, dy) px, filling exposed edges by replication."""
38	    h, w = img.shape[:2]
39	    padded = np.pad(img, ((abs(dy), abs(dy)), (abs(dx), abs(dx)), (0, 0)), mode="edge")
40	    y0, x0 = abs(dy) - dy, abs(dx) - dx
41	    return padded[y0 : y0 + h, x0 : x0 + w]
42	
43	
44	def rescale(img: np.ndarray, factor: float) -> np.ndarray:
45	    """Zoom about the centre by `factor`, then centre-crop/pad back to the
46	    original size (factor>1 = overscan crop, factor<1 = borders appear)."""
47	    h, w = img.shape[:2]
48	    nw, nh = max(1, round(w * factor)), max(1, round(h * factor))
49	    im = Image.fromarray(img, mode="RGB").resize((nw, nh), Image.BILINEAR)
50	    scaled = np.asarray(im, dtype=np.uint8)
51	
52	    out = np.empty_like(img)
53	    # x axis
54	    if nw >= w:
55	        sx = (nw - w) // 2
56	        xs_src, xs_dst, cw = sx, 0, w
57	    else:
58	        dx = (w - nw) // 2
59	        xs_src, xs_dst, cw = 0, dx, nw
60	    if nh >= h:
61	        sy = (nh - h) // 2
62	        ys_src, ys_dst, ch = sy, 0, h
63	    else:
64	        dy = (h - nh) // 2
65	        ys_src, ys_dst, ch = 0, dy, nh
66	
67	    if nw < w or nh < h:  # borders exposed — fill by edge replication
68	        edge = np.pad(scaled, ((0, 0), (0, 0), (0, 0)), mode="edge")
69	        out[:] = np.pad(
70	            edge,
71	            ((ys_dst, h - ys_dst - ch), (xs_dst, w - xs_dst - cw), (0, 0)),
72	            mode="edge",
73	        )
74	    else:
75	        out[ys_dst : ys_dst + ch, xs_dst : xs_dst + cw] = scaled[
76	            ys_src : ys_src + ch, xs_src : xs_src + cw
77	        ]
78	    return out
79

81	def envelope(img: np.ndarray, rng: np.random.Generator) -> Iterator[tuple[str, str, np.ndarray]]:
82	    """Yield (category, name, perturbed_image) over a fixed slop battery."""
83	    yield "gain", "gain-0.85", adjust_gain(img, 0.85)

85	    yield "offset", "offset-neg20", adjust_offset(img, -20)

"""Offline proof of scoreboard-chrome presence as the gameplay-screen test.

Idea under test: a gameplay screen is identified not by a whole-frame centroid
(flaky — most of the frame is dynamic) but by the presence of its static scoring
chrome. 1-player shows one bottom-left score block (score.py / SCORE_CHROME_BOX);
2-player shows two top amp panels (amp2p.py / AMP2P_BLOCK). Three masked,
per-frame-normalized SAD probes run over the whole labelled corpus.

A frame reads:
  1p present   iff  p1              <= TAU        (bottom score block)
  2p present   iff  max(pL, pR)     <= TAU        (both top amp panels)
  not gameplay iff  neither fires

Each probe = min masked normalized SAD over a small integer offset search, divided
by the masked-pixel count so the three probes are comparable (per-frame zero-mean/
unit-std normalize => ~0.0 identical shape, ~1.0 unrelated).

Passes: (1) clean per-class distribution; (2) A2D-slop robustness over perturb.py's
envelope — present must stay present, absent must stay absent; (3) a recommended
TAU with its margin.

Run: uv run python scan_scoreboard_presence.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

from gameplay import amp2p, perturb, score
from gameplay.corpus import load_corpus, load_score_corpus

SEARCH = 4          # integer offset search radius (±SEARCH in x and y)
GAMEPLAY = ("in_song", "in_song_2p")


def _min_sad_per_px(block_luma_fn, ref_n, mask) -> float:
    npix = int(mask.sum())
    best = None
    for dy in range(-SEARCH, SEARCH + 1):
        for dx in range(-SEARCH, SEARCH + 1):
            tn = score._norm_masked(block_luma_fn(dx, dy), mask)
            sad = float(np.abs((tn - ref_n)[mask]).sum())
            if best is None or sad < best:
                best = sad
    return best / npix


def build_probe():
    score_imgs = [s.image for s in load_score_corpus()]
    if not score_imgs:
        raise SystemExit("no 1p score corpus frames (data/scores/score__*.png)")
    chrome = score.build_chrome_reference(score_imgs)
    ref1p_n = score._norm_masked(chrome.ref, chrome.mask)

    refL, refR = amp2p.build_reference("left"), amp2p.build_reference("right")
    refL_n = amp2p._norm_masked(refL.ref, refL.mask)
    refR_n = amp2p._norm_masked(refR.ref, refR.mask)

    def probe(img):
        p1 = _min_sad_per_px(lambda dx, dy: score._block_luma(img, dx, dy), ref1p_n, chrome.mask)
        pl = _min_sad_per_px(lambda dx, dy: amp2p._block_luma(img, "left", dx, dy), refL_n, refL.mask)
        pr = _min_sad_per_px(lambda dx, dy: amp2p._block_luma(img, "right", dx, dy), refR_n, refR.mask)
        return p1, pl, pr

    return probe


def match_score(sid: str, p) -> float:
    """The SAD that must be LOW for this frame to read as its (gameplay) class."""
    p1, pl, pr = p
    return p1 if sid == "in_song" else max(pl, pr)  # 2p requires both amps


def fire_proximity(p) -> float:
    """Lowest SAD any gameplay rule sees — how close a frame is to reading gameplay."""
    p1, pl, pr = p
    return min(p1, max(pl, pr))


def main():
    probe = build_probe()
    samples = load_corpus()  # full 720x480 frames only (score/streak are block crops)
    by_class: dict[str, list] = {}
    for s in samples:
        by_class.setdefault(s.screen_id, []).append((s, probe(s.image)))

    # ── Pass 1: clean per-class distribution ─────────────────────────────────
    print(f"SAD-per-masked-pixel, clean (min over ±{SEARCH} search). Low = chrome present.\n")
    print(f"{'screen':<20} {'n':>3}   {'1p  min/med/max':>21}   {'2pL min/med/max':>21}   {'2pR min/med/max':>21}")
    print("-" * 96)

    def fmt(v):
        a = np.array(v)
        return f"{a.min():6.2f} {np.median(a):6.2f} {a.max():6.2f}"

    for sid in sorted(by_class):
        rows = [p for _, p in by_class[sid]]
        print(f"{sid:<20} {len(rows):>3}   "
              f"{fmt([r[0] for r in rows]):>21}   "
              f"{fmt([r[1] for r in rows]):>21}   {fmt([r[2] for r in rows]):>21}")

    # ── Pass 2: A2D-slop robustness over the envelope battery ────────────────
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    worst_present = 0.0                 # highest match_score a gameplay frame reaches
    best_absent = float("inf")          # lowest fire_proximity a non-gameplay frame reaches
    worst_present_where = best_absent_where = ""
    present_by_cat: dict[str, float] = {}
    absent_by_cat: dict[str, float] = {}

    for sid, rows in by_class.items():
        gameplay = sid in GAMEPLAY
        for s, _ in rows:
            variants = [("clean", "clean", s.image)] + list(perturb.envelope(s.image, rng))
            for cat, _name, img in variants:
                p = probe(img)
                if gameplay:
                    ms = match_score(sid, p)
                    present_by_cat[cat] = max(present_by_cat.get(cat, 0.0), ms)
                    if ms > worst_present:
                        worst_present, worst_present_where = ms, f"{sid}/{cat}"
                else:
                    fp = fire_proximity(p)
                    absent_by_cat[cat] = min(absent_by_cat.get(cat, float("inf")), fp)
                    if fp < best_absent:
                        best_absent, best_absent_where = fp, f"{sid}/{cat}"

    print("\nA2D-slop robustness (worst case over all frames + perturb.envelope):")
    print(f"  worst PRESENT match_score (must stay low):  {worst_present:.2f}  @ {worst_present_where}")
    print(f"  best  ABSENT fire_proximity (must stay high): {best_absent:.2f}  @ {best_absent_where}")

    print("\n  per-category  worst-present / best-absent:")
    for cat in ["clean", "gain", "offset", "noise", "translate", "scale"]:
        wp = present_by_cat.get(cat)
        ba = absent_by_cat.get(cat)
        print(f"    {cat:<10} {('%.2f'%wp) if wp is not None else '  - ':>6}  /  {('%.2f'%ba) if ba is not None else '  - ':>6}")

    # ── Pass 3: recommended threshold ────────────────────────────────────────
    if worst_present < best_absent:
        tau = float(np.sqrt(worst_present * best_absent))  # geometric midpoint
        print(f"\nRecommended TAU = {tau:.2f}  (geo-mean of {worst_present:.2f} and {best_absent:.2f})")
        print(f"  margin: present ≤ {worst_present:.2f}  <  TAU {tau:.2f}  <  absent ≥ {best_absent:.2f}"
              f"   (ratio {best_absent / worst_present:.1f}x)")
    else:
        print(f"\n*** NO SEPARATION: worst present {worst_present:.2f} >= best absent {best_absent:.2f} ***")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

## Proven offline

| axis | worst "present" | best "absent" | margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| clean | 0.04 | 0.62 | **15×** |
| gain / offset / noise (value slop) | 0.22 | 0.62 | **2.8×** |
| translate (static, registered out) | 0.04 | 0.62 | 15× |

- **Present vs absent separates with a 2.8× margin** under every slop family the digital HDMI capture can actually produce. Even the non-applicable analog-overscan stress doesn't invert it.
- **1p vs 2p is mutually exclusive** — bottom block fires for 1p, both amp panels for 2p, never crossed.
- **Pause overlay is safe** — the partial chrome behind a pause reads 0.62, far above TAU 0.37.
- Registration (±8, once at gameplay entry) absorbs the static rig offset; per-frame is a single masked SAD, no search.

**One honest remaining unknown:** the 5 2p frames are one session and the amp reference is in-sample, so `clean=0.04` is optimistic. The slop robustness shows the *mechanism* generalizes, but the true out-of-sample 2p margin needs real captures across matches — no synthetic perturbation substitutes for that. It doesn't block implementation (2.8× is comfortable), but it's the thing to tighten with more 2p data.

## Implementation plan (marvin)

Following the repo's host-source-of-truth → export → C → cross-check pattern:

1. **Host source of truth** — promote the probe from the scratch script into a `gameplay/present.py` module + an eval (mirrors `classifier.py`/`evaluate.py`), so the reference build + TAU live where they're tested.
2. **Export** — extend `export_c.py` to bake into `gameplay_metadata.h`: the 1p chrome ref+mask, 2p L/R ref+mask, block coords, registration search radius, and TAU (as fixed-point).
3. **C probe** — new `gameplay_present.c/.h`: integer masked normalized-SAD, register-once then per-frame evaluate. Pure C, no RTOS deps (like `gameplay_classify.c`).
4. **Integrate** — probe-first for the gameplay classes in the observe path; whole-frame centroid keeps the static screens (drop the two flaky gameplay centroids from the accept set). Register on gameplay entry.
5. **Cross-check** — extend `test_firmware_classify.py` so C == Python on the corpus, and add the present/absent eval to the suite.
6. **Journals** — record the decision in the gameplay + marvin journals.

I'll start with the host module + eval and the journal decision entry, checkpoint there, then move through export → C → integrate. Let me read the export pipeline and integration points first.

25	/* Observation is a synchronous request/response: the task idles (draining frames,
26	 * ~0 CPU) until GameplayEngine_Observe() posts a request, then classifies exactly
27	 * one fresh frame and hands the result back through s_resp_queue. There is no
28	 * free-running scan and no retained "latest" to poll — a read blocks for a frame
29	 * captured after the request, so it can never return stale state. The song_select
30	 * match is heavy soft-float (no FPU, ~tens of ms) and must never run unasked — a
31	 * continuous scan once pegged prio-4 and froze the UI. */
32	
33	static QueueHandle_t s_bus_queue;
34	static StaticQueue_t s_bus_queue_buf;
35	static uint8_t       s_bus_queue_storage[GAME_BUS_DEPTH * sizeof(game_state_t)];
36	
37	/* Response back to the single requester (the game controller). Depth 1. */
38	static QueueHandle_t s_resp_queue;
39	static StaticQueue_t s_resp_queue_buf;
40	static uint8_t       s_resp_queue_storage[1 * sizeof(game_state_t)];
41	
42	static StaticQueue_t s_frame_queue_buf;
43	static uint8_t       s_frame_queue_storage[GAME_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH * sizeof(Video_FrameInfo)];
44	
45	static StackType_t   s_task_stack[GAME_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
46	static StaticTask_t  s_task_tcb;

48	static volatile bool s_req_pending;
49	
50	/* Streak tracker state: advanced by the observer across in_song reads, reset when
51	 * gameplay is left (owned solely by game_task; not shared). */
52	static gp_streak_state_t s_streak;

54	static const char *screen_name(uint8_t idx)
55	{
56	    return (idx < GP_N_SCREENS) ? gp_screen_ids[idx] : "unknown";
57	}

59	/* Read the selection for the classified screen: static-list cell index, the
60	 * song-template index on song_select, or -1 where there's no selection concept
61	 * (gameplay / loading / unknown). `name`/`name2` receive log-friendly labels. */
62	static int16_t read_selection(const uint8_t *frame, int w, int h, uint8_t screen,
63	                              const char **name, const char **name2)
64	{
65	    *name = NULL;
66	    *name2 = NULL;
67	    const gp_menu_layout_t *menu = gp_menu_for_screen(screen);
68	    if (menu != NULL)
69	    {
70	        int cell = gp_read_selection(frame, w, h, menu);
71	        if (cell >= 0 && cell < menu->count) { *name = menu->items[cell]; }
72	        return (int16_t)cell;
73	    }
74	    if (screen == GP_SCREEN_song_select)
75	    {
76	        gp_song_t song;
77	        if (gp_read_song(frame, w, h, &song) == 0 && song.tmpl >= 0)
78	        {
79	            *name = (song.setlist == GP_SETLIST_BONUS) ? "bonus" : "main";
80	            *name2 = gp_song_templates[song.tmpl].song_id;
81	            return song.tmpl;
82	        }
83	    }
84	    return -1;
85	}

87	static void game_task(void *param)
88	{
89	    (void)param;
90	
91	    QueueHandle_t frames = xQueueCreateStatic(GAME_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH,
92	                                              sizeof(Video_FrameInfo),
93	                                              s_frame_queue_storage,
94	                                              &s_frame_queue_buf);
95	    configASSERT(frames != NULL);
96	    bool subscribed = Video_SubscribeFrames(frames);
97	    configASSERT(subscribed);
98	
99	    LOG_INFO("GAME: gameplay_engine started\r\n");
100	
101	    uint8_t   last_screen = GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN;
102	    int16_t   last_sel    = -2;  /* != any real selection or -1, so first read logs */
103	    bool      armed       = false;  /* pre-request frame discarded; next one is fresh */
104	
105	    for (;;)
106	    {
107	        Video_FrameInfo frame;
108	        if (xQueueReceive(frames, &frame, portMAX_DELAY) != pdTRUE) { continue; }
109	
110	        /* Drain every frame so the queue never backs up. Classify only while a
111	         * request is pending — no free-running scan. */
112	        if (!s_req_pending) { armed = false; continue; }
113	
114	        /* The frame in hand when the request arrived predates it; skip it so the
115	         * classified frame is guaranteed to have been captured after the request. */
116	        if (!armed) { armed = true; continue; }
117	
118	        /* A bad frame leaves the request pending so the next valid one serves it. */
119	        if (frame.buffer == NULL)                          { continue; }
120	        if (frame.bytes_per_pixel != GAME_BYTES_PER_PIXEL) { continue; }
121	
122	        TickType_t now = xTaskGetTickCount();
123	        const uint8_t *buf = (const uint8_t *)frame.buffer;
124	        int w = (int)frame.width, h = (int)frame.height;
125	
126	        int32_t best_dist = 0, margin = 0;
127	        uint8_t screen = gp_classify(buf, w, h, &best_dist, &margin);
128	
129	        const char *sel_name = NULL, *sel_name2 = NULL;
130	        int16_t sel = read_selection(buf, w, h, screen, &sel_name, &sel_name2);
131	
132	        /* In-song: read the open-ended score (training font) + multiplier + the note
133	         * streak. Sentinels (-1 / 0) elsewhere. The streak tracker is stateful: it
134	         * advances across in_song observations and resets whenever gameplay is left
135	         * (a fresh run re-seeds from the odometer). */
136	        int32_t score = -1;
137	        uint8_t multiplier = 0;
138	        uint16_t streak = 0;
139	        if (screen == GP_SCREEN_in_song)
140	        {
141	            gp_score_t sc;
142	            if (gp_read_score(buf, w, h, GP_SCORE_MODE_TRAINING, &sc) == 0) { score = sc.value; }
143	            multiplier = (uint8_t)gp_read_multiplier(buf, w, h);
144	            gp_streak_raw_t sr;
145	            if (gp_read_streak(buf, w, h, &sr) == 0) { streak = gp_streak_track(&s_streak, &sr); }
146	        }
147	        else
148	        {
149	            gp_streak_reset(&s_streak);
150	        }
151	
152	        game_state_t ev;
153	        memset(&ev, 0, sizeof(ev));
154	        ev.frame_epoch  = frame.frame_count;
155	        ev.timestamp_us = (uint64_t)now * GAME_US_PER_TICK;
156	        ev.screen       = screen;
157	        ev.best_dist    = best_dist;
158	        ev.margin       = margin;
159	        ev.selection    = sel;
160	        ev.score        = score;
161	        ev.multiplier   = multiplier;
162	        ev.streak       = streak;
163	
164	        /* Answer the requester first (clear pending before the send so a follow-up
165	         * Observe that wakes on the response can't have its new request cleared). */
166	        armed = false;
167	        taskENTER_CRITICAL();
168	        s_req_pending = false;
169	        taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
170	        (void)xQueueSend(s_resp_queue, &ev, 0);
171	
172	        if (screen != last_screen || sel != last_sel)
173	        {
174	            (void)xQueueSend(s_bus_queue, &ev, 0);
175	
176	            if (sel_name2 != NULL)  /* song_select: "<setlist> #<idx> <song>" */
177	            {
178	                LOG_INFO("GAME: %s / %s #%d %s\r\n",
179	                         screen_name(screen), sel_name,
180	                         (int)gp_song_templates[sel].index, sel_name2);
181	            }
182	            else if (sel_name != NULL)  /* static-list: "<screen> / <item>" */
183	            {
184	                LOG_INFO("GAME: %s / %s\r\n", screen_name(screen), sel_name);
185	            }
186	            else if (screen == GP_SCREEN_in_song)  /* "in_song / score N x<mult> streak<s>" */
187	            {
188	                LOG_INFO("GAME: %s / score %ld x%u streak%u\r\n",
189	                         screen_name(screen), (long)score, (unsigned)multiplier, (unsigned)streak);
190	            }
191	            else
192	            {
193	                LOG_INFO("GAME: %s\r\n", screen_name(screen));
194	            }
195	            last_screen = screen;
196	            last_sel    = sel;
197	        }
198	    }
199	}

**How should the baked scoreboard references + masks be stored in gameplay_metadata.h?**

Options:
- **int16 ref + bit-packed mask** - Normalized reference as int16 per masked pixel; mask as a packed bitmap (~2 KB total). Smallest flash, slightly more C to unpack. Matches the 'integer, exact C' convention.
- **uint8 ref + uint8 mask arrays** - Reference and mask as plain uint8 arrays over the full block (~16 KB total). Simplest C (mirrors gp_centroids), larger flash. Easiest exact cross-check.
- **float ref + bool mask** - Store normalized ref as float (like the menu baselines / song vecs already do). Soft-float SAD per frame; largest, but consistent with existing normalized-vector tables.

**Where should the 1-player reference come from, so the bake is stable?**

- **Commit a 1p chrome ref crop** - Add a committed amp2p-style crop (e.g. score_chrome_ref.png) as the fixed 1p reference, so the bake never drifts as the score corpus grows. Mirrors how amp2p_*_ref.png works.
- **Median of the score corpus** - Build the 1p reference from the median of the existing 54 score-corpus frames at bake time (reuses score.build_chrome_reference). No new asset, but the bake shifts if the corpus changes.

```text
# threshold). The threshold is a rational num/den. Grid edges and the per-cell
# coverage use one integer round-half-up rule mirrored in gameplay_score.c.

_LUMA_WI = np.array([29, 150, 77], dtype=np.int64)  # BGR weights; luma has no /256


def _luma_i(patch: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    return patch.astype(np.int64) @ _LUMA_WI


def _edge(i: int, extent: int, n: int) -> int:
    """round(i*extent/n) half-up, integer (matches gameplay_score.c gp_edge)."""
    return (2 * i * extent + n) // (2 * n)


def _cov_grid(m: np.ndarray, rows: int, cols: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Resize a cropped bool ink mask to a rows×cols uint8 coverage grid (0-255).

    Each cell = round(ink_fraction * 255) via `(count*255 + npx//2)//npx` — the
    same integer form gameplay_score.c uses.
    """
    if m.size == 0:
        return np.zeros(rows * cols, dtype=np.uint8)
    rh, rw = m.shape
    mi = m.astype(np.int64)
    g = np.empty(rows * cols, dtype=np.uint8)

def _block_luma(image: np.ndarray, dx: int = 0, dy: int = 0) -> np.ndarray:
    """Luma of the scoring block at the nominal position shifted by (dx, dy)."""
    img = _ensure_full_frame(image)
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = SCORE_BLOCK_ROI
    patch = img[y0 + dy:y1 + dy, x0 + dx:x1 + dx].astype(np.float64)
    return patch @ _LUMA_W / 256.0


def load_chrome_mask(path=None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Load the hand-drawn registration mask as a bool array at block resolution.

    The mask PNG paints the static-chrome pixels (used for registration) in
    magenta; it may be authored at any integer upscale of the block. Returns a
    (block_h, block_w) bool array.
    """
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = SCORE_BLOCK_ROI
    bw, bh = x1 - x0, y1 - y0
    p = path if path is not None else score_corpus_dir() / CHROME_MASK_FILE
    a = load_bgr(p)  # (H, W, 3) BGR; magenta is symmetric so channel order is moot
    mag = (a[..., 0] > 200) & (a[..., 2] > 200) & (a[..., 1] < 150)
    H, W = mag.shape
    if H % bh or W % bw:
        raise ValueError(f"chrome mask {W}x{H} is not an integer multiple of block {bw}x{bh}")
    fy, fx = H // bh, W // bw
    return mag.reshape(bh, fy, bw, fx).mean(axis=(1, 3)) >= 0.5


def build_chrome_reference(
    images: list[np.ndarray], config: ScoreConfig = DEFAULT_SCORE_CONFIG, mask_path=None
) -> ChromeReference:
    """Median block luma (the static chrome) + the registration mask."""
    ref = np.median(np.stack([_block_luma(im) for im in images]), axis=0)
    return ChromeReference(ref=ref, mask=load_chrome_mask(mask_path))


def _norm_masked(a: np.ndarray, mask: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Zero-mean/unit-std over the masked pixels (cancels A2D gain/offset)."""
    m = a[mask]
    return (a - m.mean()) / (m.std() + 1e-6)

```python
"""Gameplay-screen detection by static scoreboard-chrome presence.

A gameplay screen is identified by its fixed scoring chrome, not by a whole-frame
centroid: most of a gameplay frame is dynamic (scrolling note highways, animated
crowd, changing digits), so a whole-frame centroid built from a few frames matches
that one capture and drifts on any other -> intermittent UNKNOWN. The scoring
chrome is the one thing that is static, and its layout *is* the 1p/2p signature:

  1-player  -> one bottom-left score block   (SCORE_BLOCK_ROI, score.py chrome)
  2-player  -> two top amp panels            (AMP2P_BLOCK left+right, amp2p.py)

Each probe is a masked, per-frame-normalized SAD between the frame block at fixed
nominal coordinates and a committed reference crop, divided by the masked-pixel
count so the probes are comparable and the threshold is scale-free (~0 present,
~1 unrelated). The per-frame normalize (zero-mean/unit-std over the masked pixels)
cancels the analog-component value slop (gain/offset). No offset search: marvin's
capture is pixel-locked native BGR888 (capture_pipeline.md), so the chrome sits at
nominal coords; any static per-rig offset is a one-time registration concern,
deferred with the 2p digit reader (amp2p.calibrate is host-only).

Decision:
  1p present   iff  sad1p           <= TAU
  2p present   iff  max(sadL, sadR) <= TAU     (both amps must register)
  else -> not a gameplay screen (fall through to the whole-frame classifier).

TAU proven offline (fixed nominal offset, perturb.envelope value axes): worst
present 0.22, best absent 0.62 -> geo-mean 0.37. See scan_scoreboard_presence.py.
Everything is integer-luma + a single masked SAD, shaped to port 1:1 to C
(gameplay_present.c) and cross-check against it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np

from . import amp2p, score
from .corpus import load_bgr, score_corpus_dir
from .metadata import AMP2P_BLOCK, SCORE_BLOCK_ROI

# SAD-per-masked-pixel accept threshold (see module docstring).
TAU = 0.37

_LUMA = np.array([29, 150, 77], dtype=np.int64)  # BGR weights (== score._LUMA_WI)


def _luma(bgr: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Integer luma of a BGR patch (no /256 — a per-frame normalize follows)."""
    return bgr.astype(np.int64) @ _LUMA


def _norm_masked(a: np.ndarray, mask: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Zero-mean/unit-std over the masked pixels (cancels A2D gain/offset)."""
    m = a[mask]
    return (a.astype(np.float64) - m.mean()) / (m.std() + 1e-6)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Probe:
    name: str                              # "1p" | "2pL" | "2pR"
    block: tuple[int, int, int, int]       # (x0, y0, x1, y1) canonical space
    mask: np.ndarray                       # (bh, bw) bool: static-chrome pixels
    ref_n: np.ndarray                      # (bh, bw) float: masked-normalized ref luma
    npix: int


def _make_probe(name: str, block, ref_png: str, mask: np.ndarray) -> Probe:
    ref = _luma(load_bgr(score_corpus_dir() / ref_png))
    if ref.shape != mask.shape:
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: ref {ref.shape} != mask {mask.shape}")
    return Probe(name, tuple(block), mask, _norm_masked(ref, mask), int(mask.sum()))


def build_probes() -> dict[str, Probe]:
    """The three committed chrome probes (1p block, 2p left/right amp panels)."""
    return {
        "1p":  _make_probe("1p",  SCORE_BLOCK_ROI,      "score_block_ref.png", score.load_chrome_mask()),
        "2pL": _make_probe("2pL", AMP2P_BLOCK["left"],  "amp2p_left_ref.png",  amp2p.load_amp2p_mask("left")),
        "2pR": _make_probe("2pR", AMP2P_BLOCK["right"], "amp2p_right_ref.png", amp2p.load_amp2p_mask("right")),
    }


def probe_sad(image: np.ndarray, p: Probe) -> float:
    """Masked normalized SAD per masked pixel at the probe's fixed nominal block."""
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = p.block
    block = _luma(image[y0:y1, x0:x1])
    tn = _norm_masked(block, p.mask)
    return float(np.abs((tn - p.ref_n)[p.mask]).sum()) / p.npix


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Presence:
    screen_id: str | None       # "in_song" | "in_song_2p" | None (not gameplay)
    sad_1p: float
    sad_2pL: float
    sad_2pR: float


def classify_present(image: np.ndarray, probes: dict[str, Probe] | None = None,
                     tau: float = TAU) -> Presence:
    """Classify a BGR frame as 1p / 2p gameplay by scoreboard-chrome presence."""
    if probes is None:
        probes = build_probes()
    s1 = probe_sad(image, probes["1p"])
    sl = probe_sad(image, probes["2pL"])
    sr = probe_sad(image, probes["2pR"])
    two = max(sl, sr)  # 2p requires BOTH amp panels
    if s1 <= tau and s1 <= two:
        sid = "in_song"
    elif two <= tau:
        sid = "in_song_2p"
    else:
        sid = None
    return Presence(screen_id=sid, sad_1p=s1, sad_2pL=sl, sad_2pR=sr)

```python
"""Gameplay-screen detection by scoreboard-chrome presence (gameplay/present.py).

Proves the probe offline before it ports to firmware (gameplay_present.c): it must
classify every corpus frame's gameplay/not-gameplay correctly, keep "present" and
"absent" separated across the analog value-slop envelope, and leave a comfortable
margin around TAU. Positional slop (translate/scale) is excluded: marvin's capture
is pixel-locked (capture_pipeline.md), so it is a one-time registration concern,
not a per-frame effect — see scan_scoreboard_presence.py for that analysis.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

from gameplay import perturb
from gameplay.present import TAU, build_probes, classify_present, probe_sad

_GAMEPLAY = {"in_song", "in_song_2p"}
_VALUE_AXES = ("gain", "offset", "noise")  # per-frame realistic on a pixel-locked capture


def _expected(screen_id: str) -> str | None:
    return screen_id if screen_id in _GAMEPLAY else None


def test_present_classifies_corpus(corpus):
    """Every frame's gameplay/1p/2p/none decision is correct with the committed refs."""
    probes = build_probes()
    for s in corpus:
        r = classify_present(s.image, probes)
        assert r.screen_id == _expected(s.screen_id), (
            f"{s.path.name}: got {r.screen_id} "
            f"(1p={r.sad_1p:.1f} 2pL={r.sad_2pL:.1f} 2pR={r.sad_2pR:.1f}, TAU={TAU})"
        )


def test_present_value_slop_separation(corpus):
    """Under the value-slop envelope, present stays < TAU and absent stays > TAU."""
    probes = build_probes()
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    worst_present, best_absent = 0.0, float("inf")
    for s in corpus:
        variants = [s.image] + [
            img for cat, _n, img in perturb.envelope(s.image, rng) if cat in _VALUE_AXES
        ]
        for img in variants:
            s1 = probe_sad(img, probes["1p"])
            two = max(probe_sad(img, probes["2pL"]), probe_sad(img, probes["2pR"]))
            if s.screen_id in _GAMEPLAY:
                worst_present = max(worst_present, s1 if s.screen_id == "in_song" else two)
            else:
                best_absent = min(best_absent, min(s1, two))
    assert worst_present < TAU < best_absent, (
        f"no separation: present {worst_present:.1f} / TAU {TAU} / absent {best_absent:.1f}"
    )
    # Keep a real margin, not a hairline pass (proof measured ~2.9x).
    assert best_absent / worst_present > 2.0


def test_present_1p_2p_mutually_exclusive(corpus):
    """1p and 2p probes never both fire on the same frame."""
    probes = build_probes()
    for s in corpus:
        s1 = probe_sad(s.image, probes["1p"])
        two = max(probe_sad(s.image, probes["2pL"]), probe_sad(s.image, probes["2pR"]))
        assert not (s1 <= TAU and two <= TAU), f"{s.path.name}: both fired"

```

#ifndef GAMEPLAY_PRESENT_H
#define GAMEPLAY_PRESENT_H

#include <stdint.h>

/* Gameplay-screen detector by static scoreboard-chrome presence, ported from the
 * host prototype (tools/gameplay/gameplay/present.py) and driven by the generated
 * game/gameplay_metadata.h probe tables. A gameplay frame is mostly dynamic (note
 * highways, crowd, changing digits), so a whole-frame centroid is flaky; the
 * scoring chrome is the one static element and its layout is the 1p/2p signature
 * (one bottom-left score block vs two top amp panels). Pure math (no FreeRTOS /
 * video deps) so it cross-checks against Python on a host, then links unchanged
 * into the game_task. Not reentrant — uses a static block scratch; only the single
 * observer task calls it (see gameplay_classify.h). */

/* Classify a BGR888 frame (GP_CANON_W × GP_CANON_H, 3 B/pixel) as a gameplay screen
 * by scoreboard chrome. Returns GP_SCREEN_in_song (1p), GP_SCREEN_in_song_2p (2p),
 * or GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN when no chrome registers (caller falls through to the
 * whole-frame gp_classify). Fixed nominal offset, no search — the capture is
 * pixel-locked. When non-NULL, out_sad_milli[GP_N_PROBES] receives each probe's
 * L1-per-masked-pixel ×1000 (diagnostics / host cross-check). */
uint8_t gp_present(const uint8_t *frame, int width, int height, int32_t *out_sad_milli);
