```c
#include "game/gameplay_present.h"
#include "game/gameplay_metadata.h"

#include <math.h>
#include <stdint.h>

/* Standardization targets — must match gp_fingerprint (gameplay_classify.c) so the
 * probe reference (baked in the same space) compares in kind. */
#define GP_PRESENT_NORM_MEAN 128.0f
#define GP_PRESENT_NORM_STD  48.0f
#define GP_BPP               3

/* Per-block luma scratch (max block bw*bh). Luma = 29B+150G+77R ≤ 256*255 = 65280,
 * so uint16. Static — the single observer task is the only caller (see header). */
static uint16_t s_luma[GP_PROBE_MAX_LEN];

/* Masked L1 of one probe: standardize the block luma to mean128/std48 over the
 * probe's masked (static-chrome) pixels, then integer L1 vs the baked reference
 * over those pixels. Two passes over the block; stats and compare are masked. */
static int32_t gp_probe_l1(const uint8_t *frame, int width, const gp_probe_t *p)
{
    int x0 = p->block[0], y0 = p->block[1];
    int bw = p->bw, bh = p->bh;
    int n = bw * bh;

    double sum = 0.0, sumsq = 0.0;
    int cnt = 0;
    for (int r = 0; r < bh; r++)
    {
        const uint8_t *row = frame + ((uint32_t)(y0 + r) * (uint32_t)width + (uint32_t)x0) * GP_BPP;
        for (int c = 0; c < bw; c++)
        {
            const uint8_t *px = row + (uint32_t)c * GP_BPP;
            uint16_t lum = (uint16_t)(GP_PROBE_LUMA_B * px[0]
                                    + GP_PROBE_LUMA_G * px[1]
                                    + GP_PROBE_LUMA_R * px[2]);
            int i = r * bw + c;
            s_luma[i] = lum;
            if (p->mask[i]) { sum += lum; sumsq += (double)lum * (double)lum; cnt++; }
        }
    }
    if (cnt == 0) { return 0; }

    float mean = (float)(sum / (double)cnt);
    double vard = sumsq / (double)cnt - (double)mean * (double)mean;
    float std = (vard > 1e-6) ? (float)sqrt(vard) : 0.0f;

    int32_t l1 = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
        if (!p->mask[i]) { continue; }
        float v = (std > 1e-6f)
                ? ((float)s_luma[i] - mean) / std * GP_PRESENT_NORM_STD + GP_PRESENT_NORM_MEAN
                : GP_PRESENT_NORM_MEAN;
        long q = lroundf(v);
        if (q < 0)        { q = 0; }
        else if (q > 255) { q = 255; }
        int d = (int)q - (int)p->ref[i];
        l1 += (d < 0) ? -d : d;
    }
    return l1;
}

uint8_t gp_present(const uint8_t *frame, int width, int height, int32_t *out_sad_milli)
{
    if (width != GP_CANON_W || height != GP_CANON_H)
    {
        if (out_sad_milli)
        {
            for (int k = 0; k < GP_N_PROBES; k++) { out_sad_milli[k] = INT32_MAX; }
        }
        return GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN;
    }

    float pp[GP_N_PROBES];
    for (int k = 0; k < GP_N_PROBES; k++)
    {
        int32_t l1 = gp_probe_l1(frame, width, &gp_probes[k]);
        pp[k] = (float)l1 / (float)gp_probes[k].npix;
        if (out_sad_milli) { out_sad_milli[k] = (int32_t)lroundf(pp[k] * 1000.0f); }
    }

    float p1  = pp[GP_PROBE_1P];
    float two = (pp[GP_PROBE_2PL] > pp[GP_PROBE_2PR]) ? pp[GP_PROBE_2PL] : pp[GP_PROBE_2PR];

    if (p1 <= (float)GP_PRESENT_TAU && p1 <= two) { return GP_PRESENT_SCREEN_1P; }
    if (two <= (float)GP_PRESENT_TAU)             { return GP_PRESENT_SCREEN_2P; }
    return GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN;
}

```

Done — proven offline, then implemented end to end.

## What shipped

**Root cause of the 2p dropout:** every screen was classified by one whole-frame 12×8 centroid. Fine for static menus; flaky for gameplay, where most of the frame is dynamic and the `in_song_2p` centroid was trained on 5 frames of one session → drift → intermittent UNKNOWN.

**Fix — gameplay classified by static scoreboard-chrome presence** (layout *is* the 1p/2p signature; highways never enter classification):

- **Host source of truth:** [present.py](tools/gameplay/gameplay/present.py) + [test_present.py](tools/gameplay/tests/test_present.py) — three masked, per-frame-normalized SAD probes at fixed nominal coords (1p score block, 2p L/R amp panels), integer L1 in the `gp_fingerprint` mean128/std48 space, TAU = 18.
- **Export:** [export_c.py](tools/gameplay/gameplay/export_c.py) bakes `gp_probes[]` (coords, mask, uint8 reference) + `GP_PRESENT_TAU` into [gameplay_metadata.h](firmware/marvin/default/src/game/gameplay_metadata.h).
- **Firmware:** [gameplay_present.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/game/gameplay_present.c) / [.h](firmware/marvin/default/src/game/gameplay_present.h) (`-Wall -Wextra` clean); [gameplay_engine.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/game/gameplay_engine.c#L127) observe path is now probe-first, centroid for the rest.
- **Cross-check:** [test_firmware_classify.py](tools/gameplay/tests/test_firmware_classify.py) — C `gp_present` == Python on every corpus frame.

**Proof (all offline):** 0/187 corpus frames misclassified; value-slop envelope worst present 10.1 vs best absent 28.8 → **2.9× margin** around TAU 18; 1p/2p mutually exclusive; pause overlay stays absent. No registration/offset search — the capture is pixel-locked, so registration stays deferred exactly as you expected. Full host suite **80 passed**.

Journals updated in both [gameplay](tools/gameplay/docs/journal.md) and [marvin](firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md).

## Still open

- **Pending your MPLAB build + hardware validation** — a live 2p game should now hold `in_song_2p` without dropout; 1p unaffected.
- **Data gap:** the in-sample present margin (~0.04 unit-std) is optimistic because the 2p reference is a crop of one of the five 2p frames. Capturing career/quickplay 1p and cross-session 2p frames would measure the true out-of-sample margin — the slop proof shows the mechanism generalizes, but real captures are the honest confirmation.

I left [scan_scoreboard_presence.py](tools/gameplay/scan_scoreboard_presence.py) in place as the exploratory proof harness (search-radius sweep + per-category slop table). No commits made — say the word when you want them staged.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-15 20:52:21Z)**_

That clears it up — there are two conventions, and I mismatched them. Exported module APIs are PascalCase `ModuleName_Verb` (`GameplayEngine_Observe`, `Art_LoadAll`); the lowercase `gp_*` names are the pure recognizer primitives. A cross-module public entry should read like the former — that's exactly why `gp_present` looked file-local. Let me rename it `GameplayPresent_Classify` (and fix the half-applied edit + call site + test driver). The static helper `gp_probe_l1` stays lowercase — it genuinely is file-local.

marvin: classify gameplay screens by scoreboard-chrome presence

The 2-player in_song_2p screen classification intermittently dropped out.
Every screen — menu and gameplay — was classified by one whole-frame 12x8
centroid. Menus are ~static so that holds; a gameplay frame is mostly dynamic
(scrolling note highways, animated crowd, changing digits), and the in_song_2p
centroid was trained on 5 frames of one session, so a different song/stage/
character drifts many cells past t_abs / collapses the margin -> UNKNOWN.

Identify the gameplay screens by their one static element instead — the scoring
chrome, whose layout is itself the 1p/2p signature (one bottom-left score block
vs two top amp panels). New gameplay_present.c: three masked, per-frame-
normalized SAD probes at fixed nominal coords (mean128/std48 quantize as
gp_fingerprint -> integer L1 over the mask, / npix). GameplayPresent_Classify()
returns in_song / in_song_2p / UNKNOWN; the observe path runs it probe-first and
falls back to gp_classify for the static screens. No offset search / registration
— the capture is pixel-locked, so any static offset is a one-time concern
(deferred with the 2p digit reader).

Proven offline first (host tools/gameplay, source of truth present.py): 0/187
corpus frames misclassified; value-slop envelope worst present 10.1 vs best
absent 28.8 -> 2.9x margin around TAU 18; C == Python on every corpus frame
(test_firmware_classify present mode). Full host suite 80 passed.

Pending MPLAB build + hardware validation. Data follow-up: the in-sample present
margin (~0.04) is optimistic — capture career/quickplay 1p and cross-session 2p
to measure the true out-of-sample margin.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-15 21:21:22Z)**_

Here's the full map of `game/`, its boundaries, and a concrete cleanup scheme.

## 1. File inventory

| File | Role | Public prefix | Visibility |
|---|---|---|---|
| **gameplay_engine.{c,h}** | FreeRTOS `game_task`: subscribes to frames, runs the recognizer, publishes `game_state_t` on a bus, synchronous `Observe()` | `GameplayEngine_`, `game_state_t` | **external API** (task + bus) |
| **game_controller.{c,h}** | FreeRTOS controller task: menu nav + play, drives actuator, consumes `Observe()` | `GameController_` | **external API** (task) |
| **timing_pipeline.{c,h}** | Decide layer (§4.4): detector→actuator scheduling state machine | `TimingPipeline_` | **external API** (enable/disable) |
| **selection.{c,h}** | Committed user selection (song/difficulty/mode), set by UI, read by controller | `Selection_`, `selection_t`, `sel_*` | **external** shared state |
| **catalog.{c,h}** | Song-label catalog from SD, keyed by `(setlist,index)` | `Catalog_`, `catalog_entry_t` | **external API** |
| **art.{c,h}** | Album-art DDR cache (decoded covers) | `Art_` | **external API** |
| **fret.h** | `fret_t` enum (GREEN…ORANGE) | `fret_t`, `FRET_*` | **cross-cutting type** |
| gameplay_classify.{c,h} | Whole-frame centroid screen classifier | `gp_classify`, `gp_fingerprint` | **internal** recognizer |
| gameplay_present.{c,h} | Scoreboard-chrome gameplay detector | `GameplayPresent_Classify` ⚠️ | **internal** recognizer |
| gameplay_select.{c,h} | Static-list highlight + song_select readers | `gp_read_selection`, `gp_read_song`, `gp_menu_*` | **internal** recognizer |
| gameplay_score.{c,h} | In-song score/multiplier/streak readers + tracker | `gp_read_score/…`, `gp_streak_*` | **internal** recognizer |
| gameplay_metadata.h | Generated tables (centroids, geometry, probes, …) | `gp_*`, `GP_*` | **internal**, generated by `export_c.py` |

## 2. The `game/` external interface (what the rest of marvin depends on)

Measured from includes + symbol use. Everything outside `game/` touches **only** these:

- **`Art_*`** ← app, console, ui/ui_manager, ui/dashboard, ui/song_select
- **`Catalog_*`** ← app, console, ui/dashboard, ui/song_select
- **`Selection_*`** ← console, ui/dashboard, ui/song_select
- **`GameController_*`** ← app, console, ui/dashboard
- **`TimingPipeline_*`** ← app, console, actuator/manual_control
- **`GameplayEngine_*` / `game_state_t`** ← app, detector
- **`fret_t`** ← detector, actuator, perf_log, console *(the widest-used symbol in the whole module)*

## 3. Internal-only (the recognizer library)

`gameplay_classify` / `gameplay_present` / `gameplay_select` / `gameplay_score` / `gameplay_metadata` are **never included outside `game/`** — confirmed zero external includes. They're a pure, Python-mirrored recognizer library consumed by exactly one caller: `gameplay_engine.c`. Clean boundary already.

## 4. Problems

1. **Prefix zoo on the public surface:** `Art_`, `Catalog_`, `Selection_`, `TimingPipeline_`, `GameController_`, `GameplayEngine_` — six unrelated prefixes for one module. `Art`/`Catalog`/`Selection` are too generic (collision-prone, don't signal "game").
2. **Two "game" spellings:** `Game*` (controller) vs `Gameplay*`/`gp_` (engine + recognizer). Pick one.
3. **`GameplayPresent_Classify` is the odd one out** — the interface map shows it's **internal** (only the engine calls it), so it should match its siblings `gp_classify`/`gp_read_*`, *not* the public `ModuleName_Verb` style. My earlier rename was backwards; the analysis now says revert it to the `gp_` family.
4. **`fret.h` doesn't belong in `game/`** — `fret_t` is a hardware/domain primitive used by detector, actuator, perf_log, console; game is a minority user. It's parked here only so detector/actuator don't depend on each other.
5. **Header guards are inconsistent:** `GAME_FRET_H`, `MARVIN_GAME_SELECTION_H`, `TIMING_PIPELINE_H`, `GAMEPLAY_PRESENT_H`.

## 5. Proposed scheme

A clean **two-tier rule** (visibility decides the prefix):

- **Public surface → `Game<Area>_Verb`** (PascalCase):

Good question — right now the filenames don't match the symbols (`art.c` holds `GameArt_`, etc.). There's actually an elegant scheme that makes the **filename prefix mirror the two symbol tiers**:

- **`game_*.{c,h}` = public module** (holds `Game*` symbols)
- **`gameplay_*.{c,h}` = internal recognizer** (holds `gp_*`/`GP_*` symbols)

So "game" = the public API you call; "gameplay" = the vision recognizer that watches the *gameplay screen*. That maps 1:1 to the `Game*`/`gp_` symbol rule we just set.

Under that:

| Current | → | New | Symbols |
|---|---|---|---|
| `art.{c,h}` | → | `game_art.{c,h}` | `GameArt_` |
| `catalog.{c,h}` | → | `game_catalog.{c,h}` | `GameCatalog_` |
| `selection.{c,h}` | → | `game_selection.{c,h}` | `GameSelection_` |
| `timing_pipeline.{c,h}` | → | `game_timing.{c,h}` | `GameTiming_` |
| `game_controller.{c,h}` | — | *(already conformant)* | `GameController_` |
| `gameplay_engine.{c,h}` | → | `game_engine.{c,h}` | `GameEngine_` ⚠️ |
| `gameplay_classify/present/select/score.{c,h}`, `gameplay_metadata.h` | — | *(keep — recognizer)* | `gp_*` |

The one consequence to flag: for `gameplay_engine.c` → `game_engine.c` to be consistent, its symbol should also become `GameEngine_` (the rename I earlier skipped). If we move the file but keep `GameplayEngine_`, the file/symbol mismatch just reappears. So this is a package deal: **rename the engine file *and* symbol, or leave the engine entirely as `gameplay_engine.c`/`GameplayEngine_`** (in which case it's the lone public thing under a `gameplay_` filename — slightly muddies the mnemonic but is the least churn).

Blast radius (mechanical): each rename updates `git mv` + its `#include "game/…"` sites + `user.cmake` + header guard. The engine adds `app.c`+`detector` includes and the `GameplayEngine_`→`GameEngine_` symbol (13 hits/4 files).

My recommendation: do the full scheme including `game_engine`/`GameEngine_` — it's the version where the rule is airtight and nothing mismatches. Want me to run it that way, or keep `gameplay_engine`/`GameplayEngine_` untouched and rename only the other four files?
